summary: Implemented all WP-004 requirements in updateWorkPackageStatus: BLOCKED→BLOCKED blocker replacement with PM/assignee guard and dependency-type guard (step 1a); READY→IN_PROGRESS redirect to claimWorkPackage (step 1b); IN_PROGRESS→READY pipeline guard rejecting if active pipeline exists (step 5a); →COMPLETE freshness check verifying doc PASS post-dates impl start (step 5b); status_changed_at set on every transition including BLOCKED→BLOCKED early return (steps 1a and 6); IN_PROGRESS→BLOCKED and IN_PROGRESS→CANCELLED pipeline auto-cancellation with auto_cancelled:true (steps 8a/8b); IN_PROGRESS→READY unclaim clearing assigned_to in both WP detail and root index (step 8c); COMPLETE→IN_PROGRESS resets rework_counts, rework_count, and root.synthesis_generated plus revision increment (step 9). Added _ledgerRoot parameter to updateWorkPackageStatus and propagateDependencyReblock for test isolation. Exported updateWorkPackageStatus via _internal for integration testing. Added 34 new tests (inline replicas + integration). All 679 tests pass, 0 TypeScript errors.

comments.note: mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts: propagateDependencyReblock previously used withLock(projectPath, ...) as the lock directory. The original code is in the same file as propagateDependencyUnblock which correctly uses ledgerRoot ?? projectPath. The inconsistency meant that in production (where ledgerRoot != projectPath) the two functions stored data at different paths but locked different directories. Fixed to use lockDir = ledgerRoot ?? projectPath for consistency.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts: The stepNumbering in updateWorkPackageStatus has a duplicate '// 9.' comment (one for 'Handle COMPLETE -> IN_PROGRESS' and one for 'Update root index summary'). Renumbered to 9/10/11/12 in this WP, but the original duplication was a minor maintenance hazard for future contributors.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts: The BLOCKED→BLOCKED early return (step 1a) bypasses the root index summary status update (step 10). This is intentional since status doesn't change on a BLOCKED→BLOCKED transition, but the code comment could explicitly note this to prevent future confusion about whether the summary update was omitted intentionally.

mcp-server/tests/tools/work-package.test.ts: Most guard tests use inline replicas of the production logic rather than calling the real function. This pattern is consistent with the existing test file, but means that if the production code diverges from the replica, the tests will still pass. The integration tests added in this WP partially address this by testing the full function path for side-effect-heavy behaviors.

comments.note: mcp-server/tests/tools/work-package.test.ts: The auto-cancellation integration tests (§8a/§8b) each use a single IN_PROGRESS pipeline. The production code correctly handles multiple concurrent pipelines via filter+for, but there is no test exercising simultaneous cancellation of two IN_PROGRESS pipelines. Low risk — code path is straightforward — but a multi-pipeline cancellation test would remove the implicit assumption.

summary: Reviewed all 10 ACs for updateWorkPackageStatus guard work. Code is structurally sound with clear step comments, consistent _ledgerRoot parameter threading, and well-isolated integration tests. No blocking issues found. Four non-blocking suggestions recorded as comments below.

comments.note: mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts propagateDependencyReblock (~L851): newly-blocked WPs do not get wpDetail.status_changed_at = now() set. Every status mutation in updateWorkPackageStatus sets status_changed_at (including BLOCKED→BLOCKED early return), but the cascade helper is inconsistent. propagateDependencyUnblock has the same omission, so this is a pre-existing systemic gap — but as new code, propagateDependencyReblock should set it to maintain the 'status_changed_at on every transition' invariant.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts steps 8a/8b (L630–L652): Two nearly-identical blocks auto-cancel IN_PROGRESS pipelines for IN_PROGRESS→BLOCKED and IN_PROGRESS→CANCELLED. Only the summary string label differs. Could be unified into a single block: 'if (oldStatus === IN_PROGRESS && (newStatus === BLOCKED || newStatus === CANCELLED))' with a computed label. Minor DRY concern; not worth a rework but worth addressing in a future debt pass.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts _internal export (L62): propagateDependencyReblock is not exported via _internal, limiting direct unit-test isolation. Integration coverage via updateWorkPackageStatus is sufficient for now, but exporting it alongside propagateDependencyUnblock would allow targeted tests when the cascade logic grows more complex.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts UpdateWorkPackageStatusSchema status .describe() (L440): The schema description lists all legal transitions but omits BLOCKED → BLOCKED as a valid same-status blocker-replacement operation. Agents scanning the description for supported operations would not know this path exists. Adding '…BLOCKED → BLOCKED (blocker replacement)' to the description improves discoverability.
